h4_1_density_steps.name: Permutation test, steps by label density group
h4_1_density_steps.note: p from 10,000 label permutations using the (r+1)/(m+1) convention; CI from 2,000 bootstrap replicates. Cliff's delta = 0.059 (negligible), a rank-based effect size robust to the skew in step counts.
h4_1_density_steps.apa: diff = 0.322, p < .001, difference in mean steps = 0.322, 95% CI [0.130, 0.503], Cliff's delta = 0.059, N = 7,619
h4_1_density_steps.hypothesis: H4.1. Episodes on screens with lower label density take more steps to complete.

h4_2_density_adjusted.name: Negative binomial regression (adjusted)
h4_2_density_adjusted.note: Adjusted for log element count. The IRR is the multiplicative change in expected steps per unit of label density, i.e. moving from none labelled to all labelled.
h4_2_density_adjusted.hypothesis: H4.2. The association between label density and demonstration length survives adjustment for screen complexity.

h4_2_model_2.name: Negative binomial, Model 2
h4_2_model_2.note: Density measured on all visited screens; covariates: log elements (episode total), split; standard errors clustered by app.
h4_2_model_2.hypothesis: Model 2. Label density is associated with demonstration length under this specification.

h4_2_model_3.name: Negative binomial, Model 3
h4_2_model_3.note: Density measured on first in-app screen; covariates: log elements (same screen), split; standard errors clustered by app.
h4_2_model_3.hypothesis: Model 3. Label density is associated with demonstration length under this specification.

h4_2_check_a.name: Negative binomial, Check A
h4_2_check_a.note: Density measured on first screen; covariates: log elements (same screen), split; standard errors clustered by app.
h4_2_check_a.hypothesis: Check A. Label density is associated with demonstration length under this specification.

h4_2_check_b.note: Density measured on first in-app screen; covariates: log elements (episode total), split; standard errors clustered by app.
h4_2_check_b.hypothesis: Check B. Label density is associated with demonstration length under this specification.

h4_2_check_d.name: Negative binomial, Check D
h4_2_check_d.note: Density measured on first screen; covariates: log elements (episode total), split; standard errors clustered by app.

h4_3_subsplit_density.name: Chi-square test of independence
h4_3_subsplit_density.note: Cramer's V CI from 2,000 parametric bootstrap replicates.

notes: If agent rollouts become available, the same script takes an agent-success outcome by swapping the 'steps' column for a binary success column and the negative binomial for a logistic model.
limitations: The outcome is demonstration length, not agent success. AndroidControl contains human demonstrations and no agent rollouts, so no claim about agent accuracy can be made from the episode-level models here.

Demonstration length is a coarse difficulty proxy. A long demonstration may reflect a complex goal rather than a hard interface, and label density is measured over the whole episode rather than at the moment of each decision.

Models 1 and 2 adjust for the log of the total number of elements across an episode's screens. That total grows with the number of screens visited, so it partly measures the outcome, and the association they show should not be read as a finding. Model 3 takes density and element count from one screen fixed before the demonstration and is the specification to report.
The subsplit analysis is ecological: it compares aggregate label density with aggregate published accuracy. An association at split level does not establish one at episode level.
